questions.question: Which of the following Harappan sites has yielded direct archaeological evidence of a ploughed field?
questions.explanation: Archaeological excavations at Kalibangan in Rajasthan revealed evidence of a ploughed field associated with Early Harappan levels, showing two sets of intersecting furrows.

questions.question: The massive brick dockyard discovered in the Harappan civilization was located at which port town?
questions.explanation: Lothal, situated near the Gulf of Khambhat in Gujarat, possessed a large tidal dockyard basin made of burnt bricks used for maritime trade.

questions.question: Which Harappan settlement was almost exclusively devoted to craft production, including bead-making, shell-cutting, and seal-making?
questions.explanation: Chanhudaro was a tiny settlement of less than 7 hectares dedicated almost entirely to specialized artisanal craft production like bead-making and shell-cutting.

questions.question: In the drainage system of Mohenjodaro, domestic wastewater was channeled from household bathrooms directly into:
options: A) Deep soak pits dug beneath private courtyards
B) Open agricultural irrigation ditches outside the town
C) Elevated wooden aqueducts running over roof terraces
D) Covered street drains connected to main sewer channels beneath roadways
questions.explanation: Every Harappan house had drains connecting through the outer wall to street drains laid out on a grid pattern, which were covered with bricks or stone slabs.

questions.sub_topic: Political and Economic Systems in Early States
questions.question: Who was the British East India Company officer who successfully deciphered the Brahmi and Kharosthi scripts in 1838?
questions.explanation: James Prinsep, an officer in the mint of the East India Company, deciphered Brahmi and Kharosthi in 1838, unlocking ancient Ashokan inscriptions.

questions.sub_topic: Political and Economic Systems in Early States
questions.question: In ancient India, the term "Mahajanapada" referred to:
options: A) A monastic residential complex for Buddhist monks
B) Major regional territorial states that emerged around the sixth century BCE
C) A guild of long-distance maritime merchants
D) Royal officers appointed to distribute grain relief
questions.explanation: Early Buddhist and Jaina texts mention sixteen major territorial states known as Mahajanapadas flourishing across the subcontinent in the 6th century BCE.

questions.sub_topic: Political and Economic Systems in Early States
questions.question: The title "Devanampiya Piyadassi" frequently inscribed on pillars and rocks was used by which Mauryan ruler?
questions.explanation: Emperor Ashoka used the royal titles Devanampiya ("Beloved of the Gods") and Piyadassi ("Pleasant to behold") across his pillar and rock edicts.

questions.sub_topic: Political and Economic Systems in Early States
questions.question: The Prayaga Prashasti (Allahabad Pillar inscription), extolling the military conquests of Samudragupta, was composed in classical Sanskrit by his court poet:
questions.explanation: Harishena was the court poet (sandhivigrahika) of the Gupta emperor Samudragupta who composed the eulogistic Prayaga Prashasti on the Ashokan pillar at Allahabad.

questions.question: The Critical Edition of the epic Mahabharata, running into thousands of pages over several decades, was prepared under the leadership of:
questions.explanation: In 1919, the eminent Sanskritist V.S. Sukthankar initiated and led the mammoth project to compile the Critical Edition of the Mahabharata at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute.

questions.question: Which form of marriage involves a woman having multiple husbands simultaneously, as seen in the marriage of Draupadi in the Mahabharata?
questions.explanation: Polyandry is the practice of a woman having several husbands at the same time, exemplified in the epic by Draupadis marriage to the five Pandava brothers.

questions.question: According to early Brahmanical legal texts such as the Manusmriti, what was the primary duty assigned to the Shudra varna?
options: A) Conducting Vedic sacrifices and studying the scriptures
B) Protecting the realm and engaging in warfare
C) Serving the three higher varnas without malice
D) Engaging in long-distance maritime merchandise
questions.explanation: The Dharmasutras and Dharmashastras prescribed that the only occupation for Shudras was serving the three upper varnas (Brahmanas, Kshatriyas, and Vaishyas).

questions.question: In the context of early Indian society, the term "Gotra" was named after a Vedic seer, and one of its fundamental normative rules was that:
options: A) Women retained their fathers gotra even after marriage
B) Kings were legally forbidden from having any gotra affiliation
C) Foreigners were automatically assigned the Kashyapa gotra
D) Members of the same gotra were strictly prohibited from marrying each other
questions.explanation: Brahmanical practice mandated exogamy regarding gotra: individuals of the same gotra were considered descendants of the same rishi and could not marry.

questions.question: The Sanchi Stupa, one of the most prominent surviving Buddhist monuments, is situated near Bhopal in which Indian state?
questions.explanation: The Great Stupa at Sanchi is located on a hilltop in Raisen district near Bhopal in the central Indian state of Madhya Pradesh.

questions.question: Vardhamana Mahavira is traditionally recognized as which Tirthankara in the Jain lineage of spiritual teachers?
questions.explanation: Mahavira was the 24th and last Tirthankara of Jainism, preceded by 23 earlier teachers including Parshvanatha (the 23rd) and Rishabhadeva (the 1st).

questions.question: The foundational teachings and discourses of Gautama Buddha are primarily compiled in which basket of the Tripitaka?
questions.explanation: The Sutta Pitaka contains the principal sermons, dialogues, and philosophical discourses delivered by the Buddha during his lifetime.

questions.question: In the architectural terminology of a Buddhist stupa, the hemispherical earthen mound is called the "anda", while the square balcony-like structure perched on top representing the abode of the gods is termed the:
questions.explanation: Above the hemispherical mound (anda) of the stupa stood the harmika, a balcony-like square structure representing the dwelling place of the gods, from which arose a central mast (yashti).

questions.question: The medieval traveler Al-Biruni, author of the celebrated encyclopedic work Kitab-ul-Hind, arrived in India from which Central Asian territory?
questions.explanation: Al-Biruni was born in 973 CE in Khwarizm (present-day Uzbekistan) and accompanied Sultan Mahmud of Ghazni to Punjab, where he studied Indian culture.

questions.question: The famous Moroccan globetrotter Ibn Battuta authored his detailed travel memoir in Arabic under the title:
questions.explanation: Ibn Battutas famous Arabic travelogue is called the Rihla ("The Travel"), offering vivid depictions of 14th-century social and cultural life across Africa, Asia, and India.

questions.question: Francois Bernier, the French physician and traveler who spent twelve years in India (1656-1668), was closely associated with the court of which Mughal prince?
questions.explanation: Francois Bernier was a French doctor who served as personal physician to Dara Shukoh, the eldest son of Emperor Shah Jahan, and later resided in Aurangzebs court.

questions.question: In his travelogue, Ibn Battuta observed that the postal communication system in 14th-century India functioned efficiently via two channels: the horse-post called "uluq", and the foot-post known as:
questions.explanation: Ibn Battuta documented two postal networks under Muhammad bin Tughlaq: the horse-post stationed every four miles called uluq, and the foot-post with runners stationed every mile called dawa.

questions.question: In early medieval Tamil Nadu, the Bhakti saint-poets devoted to Lord Vishnu were known as the:
questions.explanation: The Alvars were Tamil poet-saints who immersed themselves in devotion to Vishnu, while the Nayanars were devotees of Shiva.

questions.question: The Virashaiva or Lingayat movement in 12th-century Karnataka was founded by which charismatic Brahman minister?
questions.explanation: Basavanna, a minister in the Kalachuri court, spearheaded the Virashaiva (Lingayat) devotional movement worshiping Shiva as a linga worn on the body.

questions.question: The revered dargah of Khwaja Muinuddin Chishti, frequented by Emperor Akbar on multiple pilgrimages, is located in:
questions.explanation: Khwaja Muinuddin Chishti established the Chishti silsila in India, and his shrine (dargah) in Ajmer, Rajasthan, became a major pilgrimage center.

questions.question: In the Sikh tradition, the compilation of the sacred scripture Adi Granth Sahib was completed in 1604 by which Sikh Guru?
questions.explanation: The fifth Sikh Guru, Guru Arjan Dev Ji, compiled the Adi Granth in 1604, incorporating hymns of the Sikh Gurus and Bhakti-Sufi saints like Kabir, Namdev, and Baba Farid.

questions.sub_topic: Vijayanagara Empire: Politics, Economy and Architecture
questions.question: The Vijayanagara Empire was founded along the banks of the Tungabhadra river in 1336 by the two brothers:
options: B) Krishnadeva Raya and Achyuta Raya
D) Deva Raya I and Deva Raya II
questions.explanation: The Sangama brothers Harihara and Bukka established the Vijayanagara Empire in 1336 CE on the southern bank of the Tungabhadra River.

questions.sub_topic: Vijayanagara Empire: Politics, Economy and Architecture
questions.question: The most celebrated ruler of the Vijayanagara Empire, Krishnadeva Raya, belonged to which ruling dynasty?
questions.explanation: Krishnadeva Raya (reigned 1509-1529 CE), who expanded the empires boundaries and authored Amuktamalyada, belonged to the Tuluva dynasty.

questions.sub_topic: Vijayanagara Empire: Politics, Economy and Architecture
questions.question: The disastrous Battle of Talikota (Rakshasi-Tangadi), which led to the sacking of Vijayanagara city, occurred in the year:
questions.explanation: In 1565 CE, the combined forces of the Deccan Sultanates (Bijapur, Golconda, and Ahmadnagar) defeated the Vijayanagara army under Rama Raya at Talikota.

questions.sub_topic: Vijayanagara Empire: Politics, Economy and Architecture
questions.question: In the administrative system of the Vijayanagara Empire, the "Amara-Nayakas" were military commanders who held territories and were required to:
options: A) Supervise naval shipyards on the Coromandel coast exclusively
B) Oversee temple priests and conduct daily ritual worship
C) Transcribe royal court poetry into Sanskrit and Kannada
D) Collect revenue from peasants and maintain a contingent of horses and foot soldiers for the king
questions.explanation: The Amara-Nayaka system was a key political innovation of Vijayanagara derived from the Delhi Sultanates iqta system, where military chiefs collected revenue and supplied troops.

questions.sub_topic: The Mughal Empire and Agrarian Society
questions.question: The monumental administrative compilation Ain-i-Akbari, providing detailed statistical information about Akbars realm, was authored by:
questions.explanation: Abul Fazl, Akbars court historian and advisor, authored the Akbarnama, of which the third volume is the administrative compendium Ain-i-Akbari.

questions.sub_topic: The Mughal Empire and Agrarian Society
questions.question: In the Ain-i-Akbari, agricultural land that was cultivated continuously year after year without being left fallow was classified as:
questions.explanation: Under the land classification scheme documented in the Ain-i-Akbari, Polaj was land that was cultivated every year and was never allowed to lie fallow.

questions.sub_topic: The Mughal Empire and Agrarian Society
questions.question: In 17th-century Mughal agrarian terminology, the term "Jins-i-Kamil" referred specifically to:
options: A) Inferior coarse millets grown in arid wasteland
B) Grain collected exclusively for village priests
C) High-value commercial cash crops like cotton and sugarcane
D) Fodder crops cultivated for imperial war horses
questions.explanation: The Mughal state encouraged the production of Jins-i-Kamil (literally "perfect crops"), which were high-earning commercial cash crops like cotton and sugarcane.

questions.sub_topic: The Mughal Empire and Agrarian Society
questions.question: In 16th-17th century rural India, the headman of the village panchayat was known locally as the:
questions.explanation: Village panchayats were headed by a headman known as the muqaddam or mandal, who was chosen through consensus of village elders and confirmed by the zamindar.

questions.question: The Permanent Settlement of land revenue was introduced in Bengal in 1793 by Governor-General:
questions.explanation: Lord Cornwallis instituted the Permanent Settlement in Bengal and Bihar in 1793, fixing land revenue in perpetuity with the zamindars.

questions.question: The "Fifth Report" on the administration of the East India Company was submitted to the British Parliament in which year?
questions.explanation: The Fifth Report was submitted to the British Parliament in 1813, containing extensive petitions, collectors reports, and revenue accounts on rural Bengal.

questions.question: In the Rajmahal Hills, the Santhal rebellion of 1855-56 was led by the legendary brothers:
options: B) Alluri Sitarama Raju and Gam Mallu Dora
D) Tilka Manjhi and Joria Santhal
questions.explanation: Sidhu and Kanhu led the Santhal insurrection (Hul) against moneylenders, zamindars, and British officials in the Damin-i-Koh region in 1855.

questions.question: The Deccan Riots Commission, formed to investigate rural peasant uprisings in western India, focused on violent unrest that broke out in 1875 in which village of Pune district?
questions.explanation: The Deccan peasant uprising started in May 1875 at the market village of Supa in Pune district, where ryots attacked moneylenders and burned debt bonds.

questions.question: The Revolt of 1857 began on 10 May 1857 with a mutiny of sepoys stationed at the cantonment town of:
questions.explanation: The mutiny erupted on the afternoon of Sunday, 10 May 1857 in the Meerut cantonment, after which the sepoys marched to Delhi.

questions.question: Who was the aged Mughal emperor whom the rebellious sepoys proclaimed as the symbolic leader of the 1857 uprising in Delhi?
questions.explanation: The sepoys converged on the Red Fort in Delhi and persuaded Bahadur Shah II (Zafar), the last Mughal ruler, to accept the nominal leadership of the revolt.

questions.question: In Lucknow, who was the deposed Nawab of Awadh whose queen Begum Hazrat Mahal rallied popular resistance against the British in 1857?
questions.explanation: Nawab Wajid Ali Shah had been deposed and exiled to Calcutta by Lord Dalhousie in 1856 on charges of "misgovernance", prompting widespread public fury in Awadh.

questions.question: The famous British painting titled "Relief of Lucknow" (1859), depicting the celebration of British colonial military victory, was painted by:
questions.explanation: Thomas Jones Barker painted Relief of Lucknow in 1859, celebrating the arrival of British reinforcements under Colin Campbell to rescue the besieged British garrison.

questions.question: In which year did Mahatma Gandhi return permanently to India from South Africa at the urging of Gopal Krishna Gokhale?
questions.explanation: Gandhiji returned to India in January 1915 after more than two decades in South Africa, where he had forged the method of Satyagraha.

questions.question: Mahatma Gandhi launched the historic Salt March to Dandi from the Sabarmati Ashram in the year:
questions.explanation: The Dandi March began on 12 March 1930 from Sabarmati Ashram, reaching the coastal village of Dandi on 6 April 1930 to break the Salt Law.

questions.question: The tragic Jallianwala Bagh massacre, which galvanized nationwide resistance and prompted Rabindranath Tagore to renounce his knighthood, took place on 13 April 1919 in:
questions.explanation: General Dyer ordered troops to fire upon an unarmed gathering on Baisakhi day at Jallianwala Bagh in Amritsar, killing hundreds of peaceful citizens.

questions.question: Mahatma Gandhi abruptly suspended the nationwide Non-Cooperation Movement in February 1922 following a violent incident at:
questions.explanation: On 4 February 1922, a crowd burned down a police station at Chauri Chaura in Gorakhpur district, Uttar Pradesh, killing 22 policemen, leading Gandhi to call off the movement.

questions.question: Who served as the Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly of India?
questions.explanation: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar served as the Chairman of the six-member Drafting Committee that prepared the Draft Constitution of independent India.

questions.question: The momentous "Objectives Resolution", laying down the ideals of the Indian Republic, was introduced in the Constituent Assembly on 13 December 1946 by:
questions.explanation: Jawaharlal Nehru moved the historic Objectives Resolution in the Constituent Assembly on 13 December 1946, outlining the basic tenets and philosophy of the Constitution.

questions.question: Who was the permanent President of the Constituent Assembly under whose signature the Constitution of India was officially adopted?
questions.explanation: Dr. Rajendra Prasad was elected permanent President of the Constituent Assembly on 11 December 1946 and presided over its historic deliberations.

questions.question: In the Constituent Assembly debates, who served as the Constitutional Advisor and prepared the initial background draft of the Constitution?
questions.explanation: Sir B.N. Rau served as the Constitutional Advisor to the Constituent Assembly, preparing comparative studies of other world constitutions and formulating the preliminary draft.

questions.question: Which raw material was imported by the Harappans from the Khetri region of Rajasthan?
questions.explanation: The Harappans sent expeditions to the Khetri region of Rajasthan to procure copper and to South India for gold.

questions.question: The collection of devotional poetry composed by the 16th-century Rajasthani poetess Mirabai was dedicated to:
questions.explanation: Mirabai was a Rajput princess who renounced royal life and composed passionate devotional bhajans expressing love for Lord Krishna.
